items.title: A CW model for the open/closed Sullivan spaces: cells indexed by Sullivan-type arc graphs, cellular gluing maps and a deformation retraction onto the subspace of unit incoming weights
items.author: Ralph M. Kaufmann
items.work: Open/Closed String Topology and Moduli Space Actions via Open/Closed Hochschild Actions
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 6 (2010) article 036, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2010.036; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition asserts three things at once about the subspace Sull_1 of the weighted open/closed Sullivan space on which every incoming window has weight one: that it is a CW complex, that it is a sub-topological quasi-PROP, and that it is a deformation retract of the full Sullivan space, with k-cells indexed by Sullivan-type arc graphs with k + 1 arcs and attaching maps given by deleting arcs. The proof has to construct the cell decomposition before passing to PMC orbits, because only then do the weighted graphs of a fixed Sullivan type form a product of simplices whose sides may still be identified by the action, giving cells C(Gamma) with interiors the products of open simplices Delta^{|{arcs incident to w}|} over the incoming windows w (source lines 1586-1597). The step that cannot be done routinely is the associativity on the nose of the induced cellular gluing maps: the author transfers it from the closed case of the cited cell-operad theorem and then argues the open case separately, since gluing keeps the punctures and the 'twisted at the boundary' condition of the closed case does not arise (source lines 1607-1610).
